source_evidence.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Centered terminal residuals give a weak forward derivative. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source_evidence.statement: Let $X_t$ be a jointly measurable process taking values in a compact state space, with almost surely continuous paths. Let $g$ be a continuous real test and $A(t,x)$ a jointly continuous real drift observable. If at each horizon the increment of $g(X_t)$ equals the time integral of $A(s,X_s)$ plus an integrable centered residual almost surely, then the time derivative of the expectation is the expectation of $A(t,X_t)$. This is the ordinary derivative at positive times and the right derivative at time zero.
assumptions: The sample space carries a probability measure. Time is nonnegative. The state space is compact and second countable, with its Borel measurable structure.
The process is jointly measurable and almost surely continuous in time. The test is continuous and the drift observable is jointly continuous.
For each nonnegative horizon there is a possibly horizon-dependent integrable real residual with mean zero. The pathwise balance with that residual holds almost surely.
source_evidence.boundary: The residual is allowed to depend on the horizon. The claim concerns the fixed test expectation.
